record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: For two vertices i and j of a graph G, let I be the set of positive real numbers β such that i and j are β-subgraph equivalent, meaning [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}. The paper proves that if I has an accumulation point, then i and j are cospectral and in fact I = R^+. Can this result be strengthened to the case where I is finite? More specifically, is there a condition on the finite cardinality M = |I| that forces i and j to be cospectral or forces I to equal all positive real numbers?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.1. Two vertices i, j of G are β-subgraph equivalent if [ eβA]ii = [eβA]jj .

Theorem 2.5. Given two vertices i, j of G, let I be the set of all β > 0 such that i and j are β-subgraph equivalent. If there is a β0 ∈ I which is an accumulation point for a sequence in I, then i and j are cospectral and I is necessarily all of R+.
It is natural to ask if this result can be improved. For example, is it still true if I is finite? Is there any condition on M = |I|, the cardinality of I, under which the result holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and for $\beta > 0$ consider the matrix exponential $e^{\beta A}$. Two vertices $i,j$ of $G$ are said to be $\beta$-subgraph equivalent if $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj}$. Vertices $i$ and $j$ are called cospectral if for every nonnegative integer $k$ one has $[A^k]_{ii} = [A^k]_{jj}$; equivalently, $[e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj}$ for all $\beta > 0$.

Fix two vertices $i,j$ of $G$ and let
$$I = \{\beta > 0 : [e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj}\}.$$
It is known that if $I$ has an accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$, then $i$ and $j$ are cospectral and $I = (0,\infty)$.

Determine whether the following finite analogue can be established: does there exist a positive integer $M_0 = M_0(G)$ (possibly depending only on the number of vertices of $G$, or on some other natural invariant) such that whenever $|I| \geq M_0$, the vertices $i$ and $j$ must be cospectral (and hence $I = (0,\infty)$)? More generally, identify any condition on the finite cardinality $M = |I|$ that forces $i$ and $j$ to be cospectral or forces $I = (0,\infty)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of this question regarding finite sets of $\beta$-subgraph equivalences and a cardinality threshold forcing cospectrality. The problem appears to remain open, with no follow-up work directly addressing the finite case identified in the literature reachable by search.
